newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-TIMELINES - Today in History - March 20.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-TIMELINES - Today in History - March 20.

text.p: ** BIRTHDAYS **

English/Australian artist and editor WILLIAM GOCHER was born on this day in 1856. In 1902, he took on the bureaucracy by wearing a neck-to-knee swimsuit and taking to the water at Manly in Sydney, at a time when daylight swimming had been banned.
Father of CORIN and VANESSA, British actor SIR MICHAEL REDGRAVE, was born in 1908.
American actress, dancer and singer GINGER ROGERS, was born VIRGINIA KATHERINE McMATH in 1911.

British singer, dubbed the "Forces' Sweetheart" because of her popularity with servicemen in World War II, DAME VERA LYNN, was born in 1917. Her biggest hits were "Auf Weidersehn (Sweetheart)" (1952), "Forget Me Not" (1952), "My Son, My Son" (1954) and her theme song "We'll Meet Again" (1954).
Circus owner STAFFORD BULLEN, whose well known Bullen Bros Circus is highly popular in Australia, was born in 1925.
American actor WILLIAM HURT was born in 1950.
American film director, actor and writer SPIKE LEE ("MALCOLM X"), was born SHELTON JACKSON LEE in 1957.
** EVENTS **
1413 : King HENRY IV of England, the first king of the
House of Lancaster, died. He had ruled since 1399.
1602 : The Dutch East India company received a charter,

granting it the monopoly on all trade between Holland and the islands between the Cape of Good Hope and the Straits of Magellan. Two years earlier, the British East India company had been formed along similar lines.
1751 : The calender in Britain was altered by an Act of
Parliament, so that from September the following year, the number of days would be moved ahead by 11 days, and the New Year would start on the 1st of January.
1792 : The French Legislative Assembly approved the use
of the guillotine as a means of conducting capital punishment.
1815 : NAPOLEON returned to Paris as a hero, putting
behind him a dreary year in exile on the Mediterranean island of Elba.
1819 : The exclusive Burlington Arcade shopping-mall
opened in London.
1841 : EDGAR ALLAN POE's detective story "THE MURDERS IN
THE RUE MORGUE" was first published, seen as a new style of writing.
1914 : Fifty tins of opium were found in the underwear of
two women on board the steamer "Empire". At the Sydney Water Police Court the pair, 35-year-old MARGARET BROWN and 37-year-old ISABELLA FLETCHER, were charged with importing opium.
1918 : Seven hundred and fifty women formed the
Australian Women's Auxiliary Army Corps.
1923 : The world's biggest pig, weighing half a ton,
arrived in Sydney from New Zealand for the Royal Show.
1933 : The first concentration camp was opened in
Germany, at Dachau.
1934 : The first practical tests of radar were carried
out at Kiel Harbour, Germany, by Dr RUDOLPH KUENHOLD.
1945 : Lord ALFRED DOUGLAS, the one time love of OSCAR
WILDE, died.
1953 : The Australian parliament passed the Television
Act, providing for both Government and commercial stations.
1969 : Beatle JOHN LENNON married YOKO ONO.
1973 : The voting age in Federal elections in Australia
was lowered from 21 to 18.
1974 : British gunman IAN BALL fired 6 shots into a car

carrying PRINCESS ANNE near Buckingham Palace, and attempted to kidnap the Princess. He was beaten off by royal bodyguards, and later captured by police after fleeing into nearby Saint James Park. The Princess was uninjured.
1983 : Australia's Father BRIAN GORE was jailed in Manila
on charges of murder and inciting rebellion. He was released in July 1984 after being exonerated. He was given an emotional homecoming in Perth on his return from the Philippines.
1995 : Up to 35,000 Turkish troops launched an attack
across the border with Iraq in pursuit of separatist Kurdish rebels.
1996 : One of Iraq's top Gulf War generals,
Staff-Lieutenant General Nazar Khazraji, defected to Jordan.
1996 : British government said for the first time that
mad cow disease could probably be transmitted to humans.

(Compiled from ABC ARCHIVES, ABC RADIO NATIONAL, "On This Day" published by REED INTERNATIONAL BOOKS LIMITED, "The Chronicle Of The 20th Century" published by PENGUIN BOOKS and "Rock And Pop (Day By Day)" published by BLANDFORD BOOKS.)
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
1989 : A tearful Prime Minister BOB HAWKE wept on
television after admitting infidelity.
1990 : Namibia gained independence from South Africa,
with SAM NUJOMA of the South West African People's Organisation (SWAPO) as Executive President.
1990 : IMELDA MARCOS went on trial in New York for fraud.
